COMPASS Skills 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 中文 · Security · License 
 

 Start here: Use & develop your own Skill ecosystem 
 
 A practical tutorial for using SKILL.md , auditing reusable skills, drafting skills with AI, extracting real workflows, and building a local Skill ecosystem.

 

COMPASS Skills gives AI agents eleven local skills: six runtime collaboration skills, two run-history skill-engineering skills, two writing and communication skills, and one local hiring-support skill. It also includes an optional Codex session-title plugin, installed separately.

The project currently ships eleven SKILL.md skills:

 Skill Purpose 
 --- --- 
 task-clarifier Aligns goals, scope, evidence, acceptance criteria, and risk boundaries before ambiguous, costly, or externally visible work. 
 task-planner Turns an agreed goal into an expandable HTML plan and updates it as the agent checks each result. 
 task-forest Maintains a repo-local task forest / DAG with goals, subtasks, dependencies, progress, deviations, todos, decisions, and conversation history. 
 pause-and-resume Cooperatively pauses unfinished work at a safe boundary and resumes it from a precise checkpoint in the same AI conversation. 
 session-handoff-prompt Compresses the current AI conversation's goal, progress, constraints, and next steps into a paste-ready prompt for a new AI conversation. 
 user-profile-keeper Maintains a local, auditable, correctable collaboration profile for communication preferences, risk style, and recurring working context. 
 run-history-skill-builder Turns completed or repeatedly refined run history into a new reusable skill package or a reviewed skill-design plan. 
 run-history-skill-upgrader Automatically turns session evidence from real execution, encountered and resolved difficulties, validation results, and user feedback into an upgrade plan for an existing skill, forming the simplest controlled self-evolution loop; it applies changes only after explicit approval. 
 clear-communication Organizes explanations, reports, comparisons, and instructions around the reader’s task while preserving facts, conditions, uncertainty, and verification state. 
 academic-humanizer Helps write or revise English and Chinese academic prose by removing formulaic AI-like patterns and restoring a natural scholarly voice while preserving claims, evidence strength, and logical relations. 
 assess-interview-candidate Turns an authorized resume and job description into an auditable evidence layer and a concise three-part offline interviewer report, with locally sanitized resume portraits and bounded timeline-age estimates kept outside scoring. 

The optional Agent Clarity title plugin lives under plugins/clarity-session-titles/ ; it has a separate installer and is not one of these eleven portable skills.

For multi-skill repositories, install only the functions you actually need. Use pause-and-resume when the same AI conversation will remain available; use session-handoff-prompt when work must move to a fresh conversation. The run-history pair supports skill engineering. Use clear-communication to organize explanations for the reader, and academic-humanizer to improve academic prose without changing its claims.

 Why COMPASS Exists

Long-running agent work needs six kinds of state:

- User context: communication preferences, risk boundaries, recurring omissions, and collaboration style.
- Project context: where the current request fits, what it depends on, and how far it has progressed.
- Goal context: how the current task contributes to the original objective and whether it still matches it.
- Pause context: the safe stopping point, remaining work, non-repeatable effects, and first action when the same AI conversation resumes.
- Handoff context: what a new AI conversation needs to continue the current task without replaying the whole transcript.
- The current plan and the evidence for changes at each checkpoint.

COMPASS organizes that state into six local workflows:

1. A local profile that the user can inspect and correct.
2. A repo-local task graph that survives AI conversation boundaries.
3. A cooperative pause checkpoint for continuing in the same AI conversation.
4. A paste-ready continuation prompt for a new AI conversation.
5. A clarification gate before ambiguous or risky execution.
6. An HTML plan that reflects completed work and any changes to the next steps.

 How The Core And Meta Skills Work Together

 task-clarifier is the entry point for ambiguous, high-cost, high-risk, evidence-sensitive, or externally visible work. It first identifies the user-owned decisions that must be made, asks up to three focused questions with recommended answers when open decisions remain, and can ask no questions when lookup resolves them. It always confirms shared understanding before searching or executing.

 task-forest records long-running work structure: why a task exists, where it fits, how far it progressed, what changed, and what remains unresolved.

 pause-and-resume stops an unfinished task at the nearest safe boundary, records what must and must not be repeated, and continues from that checkpoint when the user returns to the same AI conversation. It creates no file solely for pausing.

 session-handoff-prompt turns the current AI conversation, explicit transcripts, workspace evidence, and optional task-forest exports into a concise prompt for the next AI conversation. It reads task-forest as structured context but never modifies it.

usage.title: Example maintenance notes become a first-use explanation
usage.html:
This is a hypothetical example. A colleague asks how to start using NoteBox. The notes say:

  • Click New note to write; content saves automatically in the current browser. One real save operation has been checked.
  • The cloud-sync button exists, but its service is not connected.
  • Closing the window preserves notes. Clearing browser data deletes local notes.
  • The maintenance record also lists 23 local checks, sync_enabled=false, and a plan to organize logs later.

A reader-oriented answer is:

Open NoteBox and click New note to start writing. Your notes save automatically in the current browser; one save operation has been checked.

Cloud sync is not available yet, so you cannot rely on it to read these notes on another device.

Closing the window keeps your notes. Clearing browser data deletes the local notes.

The explanation leads with the action and keeps the storage and deletion conditions together. The internal field and maintenance count remain in the maintenance record because they do not change this reader's next action. A maintenance review could need those details again.
